summary: A real, dated Amazon rule change with visible certificate-rejection pain, but no one has been found asking for or paying for a standalone checker, and the broker who sells the policy is the default fix. $19 one-time with a short window and a thin recurring hook falls below the bar.

demand.evidence: Problem is documented (Amazon notice 4,800 views/52 replies; forum threads of repeated rejections) but RESEARCH.md admits no one is asking for or charging for a standalone checker; the forum rejections are 2-3 years old.

statusQuo.evidence: Sellers email the broker (Assureful, Next, Marsh) who bundles certificate help into the policy, or read Amazon's criteria page and forum. Cost is days of delay, not dollars.

specificity.evidence: Clear buyer: solo/2-person seller with an enhanced-safety listing holding a broker certificate and facing a deactivation deadline. No named person; the group size is unknown because the 11-category list is not public in full.

wedge.evidence: Upload, free pass/fail, $19 for the broker fix email is shippable in days. The paid piece is easy to replicate by hand, so the real narrowest test is a free checklist page with email capture.

futureFit.evidence: Brokers will standardise compliant certificates, Amazon may reword the criteria, and the need recurs once a year at most; the renewal reminder is a weak hook.

premises: Sellers are rejected for wording errors a checker could catch: supported by forum threads.
Sellers will pay a third party instead of asking their broker: not supported by any evidence.
The rule list can be maintained without Seller Central access: only nine of about 13 criteria are publicly confirmed.
Enough small sellers can be reached in communities that restrict self-promotion: plausible but unproven.
A free model can extract ACORD 25 fields at 90%+ accuracy: plausible for text PDFs, unverified.
alternatives: Minimal: free static checklist page with the nine public criteria, broker email template and email capture (S effort).
Extend David's covercheck repo with an Amazon ruleset so one extraction engine serves two buyers (M effort); the better long-term home.
Ideal: standalone checker with consultant packs, OCR and renewal reminders (L effort); builds the platform before any demand signal.
Lateral: free checker that refers failing sellers to a specialist broker for a commission (excluded in v1, and moves into insurance sales).
wedge: A single free page that checks pasted certificate text against the nine publicly confirmed criteria and produces a copy-paste broker fix email, with an email box for updates.

feasibility.notes: Next.js on Vercel/Cloudflare free, Neon free, pdf text extraction plus a free-model extraction call, deterministic TypeScript rules, Vitest with one worker. Stripe and Resend are deferred to M2/M3. The one test that proves M1: a certificate listing Amazon only as certificate holder returns fail on additional insured, and the fully compliant fixture returns zero fails. Concern: free-model extraction accuracy on real PDFs.

risks: Willingness to pay for the check alone is unproven; the broker is the default fix.
Short window: the reported 45-day deadline lands mid-December, before a test and build would finish.
Rule drift and four unconfirmed criteria behind Seller Central sign-in.
Reach: seller forums and groups restrict self-promotion.
A false pass is only a prediction, with insurance and legal-advice liability.
Low revenue ceiling ($19 once; about $950 at 50 paid checks).
Overlap with covercheck and other compliance-checker ideas in the portfolio.
killCriteria: In a 14-day test: fewer than 50 visitors or fewer than 5 real uploads or signups; no seller reports being rejected on a broker-issued certificate; or Amazon softens the rule or brokers' default certificates already pass.
